findings.F1: The book loses through its early exits. Its 51 trades closed before 4.5 days lose -4.02 % net on average, while its 92 trades held the full 5 days earn +3.26 %. Holding those same 51 early trades for a fixed 5 days would have lost only -1.89 % (47 found), and almost all of them (47 of 51) closed because the forecast fell to 0 when the situation ended, not on a reversal of the forecast. This drain is what keeps the Sharpe 0.086 below holding's and the Calmar at 0.371.
findings.F2: The fall does not end when the close leaves the top of the range. On all 127 signal bars, the short earns 1.69 % on the first day and another 1.57 % from day 2 to day 5. Even when the first day rose (59 bars), the next four days still gave 1.34 % short, so leaving the position after a day 1 that went the wrong way gives up most of the move.
findings.F3: The size grows with the depth of the 5-day fall. On all signal bars, the unusual 5-day move in the short direction is 7.97 % (t 2.55), 7.31 % (t 3.33), 3.80 % (t 2.73) and 1.55 % (t 0.92), from the deepest 5-day fall quartile to the shallowest (30 bars each). A deep fall alone is not the effect: in-profile and out-of-profile grid cells without the signal and a 5-day fall below -5 % earn only +0.22 % (t 0.36, 477 cells).
findings.F4: The losses sit in the shallow cases. The 88 trades entered after a 5-day fall deeper than 5 % earn +2.41 % net (42 % winners, fixed 5-day hold +3.39 %). The 55 trades entered after a shallower fall lose -2.13 % (24 % winners), hold the worst trade (-62.8 %, ZEC in w11) and are negative in 6 of their 10 windows.
findings.F5: The profile carries the effect. The same situation (a negative 5-day return and a close in the upper half of the range) outside the choppy agitated profile has an unusual move of -0.26 % (t -0.37, 317 grid cells), against +12.1 % (t 3.35, 22 cells) inside it.
findings.F6: The book's gain rests on few windows, and its falls are in w11 and w12. w16 alone returns +15.4 % (13.0 bp a day), while w11 returns -2.65 % (trade mean -5.51 %) and w12 returns -1.22 % (trade mean -4.84 %). The deepest fall, -6.06 %, is in w12, against a yearly return of +3.2 %.
findings.F7: A longer horizon does not help. Holding the trades 10 days instead of 5 drops the full trades to +0.35 % and the early ones to -6.50 %, so the move lives in the 5 days after the signal.
findings.F8: The grading by nearness to the high shows in the trades. Trades in the lowest, middle and highest third of entry forecast size earn -0.39 %, +0.65 % and +1.75 % net (49, 46 and 48 trades).

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the full next five days even when the following closes leave the top of the range, and the nearer that close was to the day's high, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps the short for the whole five days from the signal instead of covering as soon as the close drops out of the upper range or the 5-day return turns up.
ideas.name: high-close fade held five days

ideas.idea: In a choppy, agitated market, when a coin's daily close sits in the upper part of that day's high-low range after its 5-day return has been negative, its price falls over the next five days, and the deeper that 5-day fall and the nearer the close to the day's high, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader sizes the short up when a close pinned near the high follows a deep 5-day fall, and keeps it small after a shallow one, where the book's losses and its worst trade sat.
ideas.name: deep-fall high-close fade
